title: Stitching Gateway Flux — API and runtime sketch
content:
Context / what this is:
Personal sketch: the idea is a small, client-facing gateway that performs "stitching" of multiple partial model responses / fragments and exposes a compact flux-style API for clients that need multi-model composition, partial re-fetch, and cheap fallbacks.

Motivation:
- Some customers want to compose output from: hosted-main LLM + private-local adapter + cached-freshening service.
- Want to minimize round-trips: gateway should produce a single streaming surface but manage multiple upstreams.
- Keep runtime lightweight (small code path) so teams can run gateway as a sidecar or managed shared pool.

Non-goals (for now):
- Full orchestration of long-running pipelines (that's job for batch/flows).
- Rewriting prompts for policy. Keep pass-through unless configured.

High-level responsibilities (gateway):
- Accept client request (single call) describing composition plan (or use policy).
- Fan-out to upstreams with per-upstream configs (timeout, max-tokens, affinity).
- Re-assemble fragments using deterministic stitch rules or heuristics.
- Expose streaming fragments to client with provenance markers and a single finalization event.
- Lightweight caching / prefix prewarm where applicable.

API shape (compact):
- POST /v1/stitch 
  body: {
    "plan_id": string,                 // optional opaque plan name
    "input": {"messages"|"prompt": ...},
    "lanes": [                         // ordered lanes to consult
      {"name":"hosted-a", "role":"primary", "model":"redwood-v2", "max_tokens":256, "timeout_ms":400},
      {"name":"local-adapter", "role":"recovery", "model":"adapter-v1", "timeout_ms":150, "affinity":"tenant"},
      {"name":"cache-fresh", "role":"cached", "policy":"prefix-only", "staleness_ms":60000}
    ],
    "stitch_policy": "first-complete|merge-chron|priority-rank",
    "stream": true|false,
    "client_labels": {"feature":"compose-notes"}  // optional telemetry tags
  }

Notes on lanes: lanes are lightweight descriptors — no heavyweight creds here; gateway maps lane->upstream using local mapping config (see runtime config).

Response streaming protocol (rough):
- chunk types: {"partial","meta","hint","final"}
- partial: {lane:, seq:, text:}  (seq increments per-lane)
- meta: {trace_id, provenance: [lanes consulted], cost_estimate}
- hint: small signals like "fallback-engaged" or "stitch-conflict"
- final: {stitch_decision: "selected-lane"|"merged", "reason": "timeout"|...}

Example stream (pseudo):
[meta]{trace_id=abc}
[partial]{lane=hosted-a,seq=1,text="Once upon"}
[partial]{lane=local-adapter,seq=1,text="Once upon a time"}
[hint]{fallback-engaged:local-adapter}
[final]{stitch_decision=merged, reason=policy-priority}

Runtime config sketch (yaml-style prose):
- mapping: lane -> endpoint (k/v)
- concurrency: per-lane inflight cap (default 128)
- backpressure: continuous-batch-window-ms, burst-limit
- retry: idempotent-only, max-attempts 1 by default for low-latency
- affinity: tenant->preferred-lane mapping (soft)

Stitch policies (brainstorm):
- first-complete: take first lane that returns a complete-ish answer (>=min_tokens)
- priority-rank: lane order defines priority, fallback to next on timeout/error
- merge-chron: merge tokens by timestamp sequence, useful when lanes return complements
- overlap-compaction: if two fragments overlap, prefer longer from higher-ranked lane; keep provenance markers

State machine (approx ascii):
CLIENT -> GATEWAY: request
GATEWAY: -> parallel: lanes (call)
lanes -> GATEWAY: partials, final, errors
GATEWAY: apply stitch policy -> emit stream to CLIENT until final

Edge cases / tricky bits:
- Partial contradictory outputs (different factual claims): need config for "fact-suppression" or to always prefer enterprise/private lane for PII-sensitive answers.
- Token accounting: merging tokens from multiple lanes complicates billing; pragmatic approach: report per-lane tokens in meta, but surface single token stream to client.
- Pause/resume: client might disconnect mid-stream; gateway should keep short-lived inflight (grace window) and optionally continue to finalize logs for observability.
- Auth: gateway may have to inject per-lane creds. For users dir sketch, assume mapping service holds secrets; gateway uses short-lived credentials.

Telemetry / observability minimal set:
- trace_id, lanes_consulted, per-lane latency, per-lane token_count, stitch_policy_used, final_decision, errors
- sample heavy: stream_size, merge_conflicts

Open questions (TODOs):
- Should the client be able to attach custom merge hooks (webhook or wasm) on a per-request basis? risk: increases attack surface and latency.
- Failure semantics: if primary returns but merged output is lower quality than fallback, how to signal, and when to prefer fallbacks? Need eval harness.
- Rate-limiting model: do we count composite request as N upstream calls for quota? likely yes but expose a "composite_cost" estimate pre-flight.
- Should we surface provenance to downstream apps in a structured way (e.g., JSON-LD) or keep lightweight markers?

Small implementation notes / experiments to try: 
- PoC: implement gateway as tiny Node/Go service with plugin points for lane adapters. Start with in-memory mapping and simple priority policy.
- Add deterministic stitch unit tests: overlapping strings, truncated tokens, mismatched punctuation.
- Build an eval dataset (50 prompts) where we expect complementary answers from two models and measure merge quality heuristics.

Next steps (for me):
- Draft PR skeleton for mapping config and simple priority stitch (target: 1-week prototype)
- Run early cadence with Maya to capture affinity rules we need for Dedicated vs Private lanes
- Make sketch of billing signals to pass back to control plane (ENG-2147 follow-up)

Notes to self / random TODO lines:
- keep stream protocol compact, avoid deeply nested json per-chunk
- revisit "merge-chron" complexity if we need token-level alignment
- check whether Console can reuse per-route dashboards for stitch decisions (cost+latency combined)

Slack refs inline: convo with #infra-gateway on 2024-10-27 about short-lived creds; mention to ping @connor when prototyping lane affinity.

End of sketch.
